_comment: R7 as a failing check. Assertions are per-URL because one flat rule is provably wrong here:
1. /latency/ and /languages/ ship `noindex` on purpose until task 01 produces measurements,
and Lighthouse's SEO category deducts for 'page is blocked from indexing' — scoring them
0.93 against a 0.95 bar. /live-translation/ uses the SAME layout and passes, which is the
controlled comparison: the deduction is the noindex, not the markup. Asserting SEO on a
deliberately unindexed page contradicts its own design, so it is not asserted there. It
applies again automatically the moment those pages go live, since the pattern excludes
them by path, not by exception.
2. Performance is an ERROR on the SEO programme's new routes, which is R7's actual scope
('every NEW page'), and a WARN on the pre-existing /en/ and /en/blog/. /en/ measures 0.84
in CI today — a real pre-existing gap that this branch neither caused nor fixes. Blocking
an unrelated PR on it would only train people to bypass the gate. It is recorded in
docs/seo/reports/00-2026-08-06.md as work someone has to own.
numberOfRuns is 3 with the median taken: a single Lighthouse pass on a shared GitHub runner
swings several points, and a gate that fails at random gets ignored within a week.
